author: Amina Yonis, PhD
text:
Note-taking is best when applied in two stages:

1) Write down the main points during the lecture/tutorial, then,

2) Go back to summarise, condense and organise the notes to be used later for writing assignments or revising.

topReplies.author: Amina Yonis, PhD
topReplies.text:
Mind Maps

These help you to get ideas on paper, make connections and provide an overview of key points. 

The basic principle is to note down the central topic or idea in the centre and work outwards adding the points which flow from and connect to it.

topReplies.author: Amina Yonis, PhD
topReplies.text:
Cornell Notes

Divide your notes into two sections: the left side for cues or main ideas and a wider space on the right side for note-taking. 

It is designed to promote active listening, critical thinking, and effective studying.

Free template download > 
https://
resources.thepagedoctor.com/l/cornellnotes

topReplies.author: Amina Yonis, PhD
topReplies.text:
The Sentence Method

This is the simplest and least structured method, useful useful for fast-paced lectures with a lot of content. 

- Write content, such as terms, facts, or ideas in sentences
- Move to the next line for each new point
- Number each new sentence as you progress

topReplies.author: Amina Yonis, PhD
topReplies.text:
The Outlining Method

This method involves writing in topics and sub-topics, and identifying them by indenting the text, numbering the lines, or using a dash or bullet point. 

This is an effective method for visual learners.

topReplies.author: Amina Yonis, PhD
topReplies.text:
The Charting Method

Using a table to make your notes with separate columns for main points, questions, details etc to classify your information for easy access. 

If you used the Outline Method in class, follow up with the Charting Method to organise and form connections.
